correctness.rationale: The Laurent exponent has an essential singularity at infinity, while its positive-axis value tends to zero because the outermost coefficient is negative. With absolute Laurent convergence this forces infinitely many coefficients of each sign for each positive time. Finite-cycle strict spectral damping implies eventual positivity. The aliasing inequality |W_n-exp(tq(b))| <= 4 exp(alpha t-sn/2), diagonal Fourier lower bound C/sqrt(t), uniform short-time negative outer stencil, and compact-time convergence imply a full no-positivity window of linear size. For the fourth-order five-point stencil exact arithmetic gives q(16)=-2475/1024, alpha<105 and c=1/500; the Fourier tail bound 2 sum_{k>=1} exp(-k^2)<1 gives H_n<=n^2/16. A freshly run standalone verifier passed 3977 assertions; these complement the analytic infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A standard fourth-order semidiscrete diffusion stencil is spectrally stable yet its spatial heat kernel has arbitrarily far positive and negative coefficients at each positive time; furthermore finite periodic grids require a dimension-proportional delay before any positivity is possible. This supplies a motivated quantitative obstruction not implied by the known qualitative eventual-positivity criterion, clarifies the inverse-elliptic-vs-semigroup distinction, and offers a directly testable benchmark for high-order positivity-preserving schemes.
